faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium sulfuric acid injection quill?
faq.a: Grade 12 Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni offers the optimal balance of strength, corrosion resistance, and fatigue life for titanium sulfuric acid injection quill.

faq.q: How is a titanium sulfuric acid injection quill manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium sulfuric acid injection quill is manufactured using Seamless tube extrusion; CNC machining; TIG welding (ERTi-2 filler); Hydrostatic testing. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 12 Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni for titanium sulfuric acid injection quill?
faq.a: Other materials such as steel or aluminum are significantly heavier and lack the corrosion resistance required for long-term service.

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium sulfuric acid injection quill?
faq.a: Titanium Sulfuric Acid Injection Quill components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348, ASME. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium sulfuric acid injection quill?
faq.a: With proper material selection (Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V) and manufacturing process control (thread rolling, heat treatment), titanium titanium sulfuric acid injection quill components exhibit excellent fatigue life and corrosion resistance in service.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium sulfuric acid injection quill?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
